title: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia Is Out After Five Days and One Briefing
excerpt: President Trump told his new press secretary to reconsider the job on Friday, hours after questions over her failed bar exam and a 14-minute debut briefing consumed her first week.
body:
• Katie Zacharia is transitioning out as White House press secretary after five days in the job, a White House official confirmed on Friday.
  • President Trump told reporters he had advised her to reconsider the role after a difficult first week; no successor or new role for Zacharia has been announced.
  • Her only briefing, on Tuesday, lasted about 14 minutes and took three questions; scrutiny then turned to her legal credentials after reports she never passed the California bar exam.
  • The vacancy opens less than three weeks before the November 3 midterm elections, with the press secretary's office as the administration's main daily channel on immigration and other policy fights.

Katie Zacharia's tenure as White House press secretary ended on Friday after five days, when a White House official confirmed she was "transitioning out" of the role shortly after President Donald Trump told reporters he had advised her to reconsider it. According to The Hill, Trump said he had told her earlier in the day that, in her position, he would reconsider.

"You don't have to do this if you don't want."

— President Donald Trump, to Katie Zacharia

A difficult first week

Zacharia, a conservative commentator who came to the White House from Trump Media & Technology Group, where she worked as a senior communications adviser, gave her first briefing on Tuesday, a day after starting the job. It lasted roughly 14 minutes, took questions from only three reporters, and broke news of its own: asked about misconduct allegations against US ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle, which Guilfoyle has denied, Zacharia said the administration had asked her to step down, and Guilfoyle announced her departure within hours. Zacharia also could not answer a question about whether the United States had stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=hhziMHhCSFE

The bar exam question

The sharper problem was her biography. Zacharia, who graduated from Pepperdine University's law school in 2011 and has identified herself as a lawyer in television appearances, was asked beside the president which state she had taken the bar exam in, and answered by referring to a move to China. The Wall Street Journal then reported she had failed the California bar exam. A watchdog group, the Campaign for Accountability, filed a complaint with the State Bar of California on Wednesday. On Fox News on Thursday, Zacharia acknowledged she had failed the exam and never retook it, while maintaining she had worked in international transactional law in China; on Friday she argued she had been hired as press secretary, not White House counsel. The Center Square reported the White House confirmed her departure the same day.

What it means

Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt, who left the post at the end of August after serving since the start of Trump's second term in January 2025, citing a wish to spend more time with family. Her exit, five days in, was quickly compared online with Anthony Scaramucci's 11 days as communications director in 2017. A senior administration official said Zacharia would move to a new role to be announced later.

What happens next

The White House has not named an acting or permanent successor. Whoever takes the podium inherits the job at its most exposed moment of the cycle: the final weeks of a midterm campaign in which the president has publicly complained that his administration is failing at public relations even as, in his words, the country has never done better.
